name: Executive order of November 16, 1874 enlarging the Colorado River reservation
nations: Colorado River Indian Tribes (Mohave, Chemehuevi, Hopi and Navajo)
promises: An enlargement, not a cession: the President enlarged the reserve established by the Act of March 3, 1865 and enlarged by the executive order of November 22, 1873 (Royce).
Royce records that the boundaries this order defined were found defective and incomplete, so it was superseded by the executive order of May 15, 1876, which correctly defined the enlarged boundaries.
landTaken: None by this order; it added land. The Indian Claims Commission found the Mohave were deprived of their Arizona and Nevada lands on March 3, 1865, the date of the Act creating the reservation, without compensation (Dockets 283 and 295); that belongs to the 1865 Act, not this order.
today: The Colorado River Indian Tribes say the reservation, created in 1865 for the Indians of the Colorado River and its tributaries, stretches along both banks of the river and includes almost 300,000 acres.

nationVoice.summary: CRIT says the reservation was created in 1865 originally for the Mohave and Chemehuevi, who had lived there for centuries, that Hopi and Navajo people were relocated there later, and that it now covers almost 300,000 acres on both sides of the river.

openQuestions: treaties.json lists Royce areas 466 (the 1865 Act), 554 (the order of November 22, 1873) and 593 (the order of May 15, 1876) for this entry; Royce gives this order no area number of its own. Not edited.
The long dispute over the reservation's western (California) boundary under the 1876 order, including Arizona v. California, was not researched here; it concerns the 1876 order.
The Mohave claims (Dockets 283 and 295) ended in compromise settlements in 1973 and 1975 per the Commission's index; the amounts were not read because they concern the 1865 taking, not this order.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Colorado River" and "Mohave" (opened 156 Ct. Cl. 712, 221 Ct. Cl. 989, 222 Ct. Cl. 690, 203 Ct. Cl. 709) and ICC full text "Colorado River reservation 1876 boundary", "Colorado River Indian Tribes 1874"; no finding about this order. The 1962 order sent to the ICC a CRIT claim that the United States settled other tribes and persons on its lands from 1942 and 1945; a stipulated judgment of $850,000 was entered on October 19, 1979 (221 Ct. Cl. 989). That is a settlement about 1940s use, not a finding about this order.

plain.promised: An enlargement, not a cession. The President added land to the Colorado River reservation; the boundaries proved faulty and were redrawn in 1876.
plain.happened: No breach of this order was found. The Indian Claims Commission found the Mohave lost their Arizona and Nevada lands without payment in 1865; that belongs to the 1865 Act.
plain.today: The Colorado River Indian Tribes say the reservation covers almost 300,000 acres along both banks of the river.
